[JEE Main 2022, 29 June (Shift 1)]

Since \(a R b\) is true if both \(a\) and \(b\) belong to the same set.

For reflexivity:

\(a R a, a \in A\), so it is true.

For symmetry:

Let \(a R b\) be true

\(\Rightarrow a\) and \(b\) belong to the same set.

\(\Rightarrow b\) and \(a\) also belong to the same set

\(\Rightarrow b R a\) will be true

For transitivity:

Let \(a R b\) and \(b R c\) be true.

\(a R b \Rightarrow a, b\) belong to the same set

\(b R c \Rightarrow b, c\) belong to the same set

If \(a, b \in A_i\) and \(b, c \in A_j\), then \(b \in A_i \cap A_j\)

Since \(A_i \cap A_j=\emptyset\) for \(i \neq j\), we must have \(i=j\)

Hence \(a, c \in A_i\)

\(\Rightarrow a\) and \(c\) belong to the same set

\(\Rightarrow\) so \(aRc\) will be true.

So \(R\) is an equivalence relation.

Let \(A =\left[a_{i j}\right]\) be a square matrix of order \(3\) such that \(a_{i j}=2^{j-i}\), for all \(i, j=1,2,3\). Then, the matrix \(A ^2+ A ^3+\) .... \(+ A ^{10}\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 June (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The \((i,j)\)-th element of \(A^2\) is

\((A^2)_{ij}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{3}a_{ik}a_{kj}\).

Since \(a_{ik}=2^{k-i}\)

and \(a_{kj}=2^{j-k}\),

we get \((A^2)_{ij}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{3}2^{k-i}2^{j-k}\).

Therefore, \((A^2)_{ij}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{3}2^{j-i}\).

Since the same term occurs three times,

\((A^2)_{ij}=3\cdot2^{j-i}\).

But \(a_{ij}=2^{j-i}\).

Hence, \((A^2)_{ij}=3a_{ij}\).

Therefore, \(A^2=3A\).

Now, \(A^3=A\cdot A^2=3A^2=3^2A\).

Similarly, \(A^4=3^3A\).

Thus, in general,

\(A^r=3^{r-1}A\) for \(r\geq1\).

Therefore, \(A^2+A^3+\cdots+A^{10}=(3+3^2+\cdots+3^9)A\).

Using the sum of a geometric progression,

\(3+3^2+\cdots+3^9=\dfrac{3(3^9-1)}{3-1}\).

Hence, \(3+3^2+\cdots+3^9=\dfrac{3^{10}-3}{2}\).

Therefore, \(A^2+A^3+\cdots+A^{10}=\dfrac{3^{10}-3}{2}A\).

Let \(b_1 b_2 b_3 b_4\) be a \(4-\)element permutation with \(b_i \in\{1,2,3, \ldots \ldots, 100\}\) for \(1 \leqslant i \leqslant 4\) and \(b_i \neq b_j\) for \(i \neq j\), such that either \(b_1, b_2, b_3\) are consecutive integers or \(b_2, b_3, b_4\) are consecutive integers. Then the number of such permutations \(b_1 b_2 b_3 b_4\) is equal to...........

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 June (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(A\) be the set of four-term permutations for which

\(b_1,b_2,b_3\) are consecutive integers in increasing order.

The first term \(b_1\) can be any integer from \(1\) to \(98\),

because the triple is \(b_1,b_1+1,b_1+2\)

After fixing this triple,

\(b_4\) can be any one of the remaining \(100-3=97\) integers.

Therefore, \(n(A)=98\times97\)

Let \(B\) be the set of four-term permutations for which

\(b_2,b_3,b_4\) are consecutive integers in increasing order.

For set \(B\),

the value of \(b_2\) can be chosen from \(1\) to \(98\),

and after fixing \(b_2,b_2+1,b_2+2\), the value of \(b_1\) has \(97\) choices.

Therefore, \(n(B)=98\times97\).

A permutation belongs to both \(A\) and \(B\) only when all four entries are consecutive integers in increasing order.

Such a permutation has the form \(k,k+1,k+2,k+3\), where \(1\leq k\leq97\)

Therefore, \(n(A\cap B)=97\)

Using the principle of inclusion and exclusion,

\(n(A\cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A\cap B)\)

Thus, \(n(A\cup B)=98\times97+98\times97-97=97(196-1)=97\times195=18915\)
